chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Mahmoud, from his father, from a man who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have washed your hand for the meal, do not wipe your hand with the towel, for the Blessing does not cease in the meal as long as the moisture remains in the hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for drying hands before eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against wiping hands with a towel immediately after washing them for a meal, stating that the blessing in the food persists as long as the natural moisture remains on the hands. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving the physical signs of divine favor (barakah) in daily rituals, linking bodily purity with spiritual sustenance. It also underscores the importance of mindful consumption, where the act of eating is accompanied by awareness of God's blessings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Abu Mahmoud, from his father, from a man who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you have washed your hands for the meal, so do not wipe your hand with the towel, for the Blessings do not cease in the meal for as long as the moisture is in the hand’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from abu Mahmud from his father from a man who has said the following:
“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’When you wash your hand for food do not wipe it with a towel because blessings continue in the food as long as hands have moisture in them/”
